cards.title: OpenAI Revenue Crosses $10B Milestone
cards.body: OpenAI's quarterly revenue hit $10 billion for the first time, representing a nearly 50% jump from $6.7 billion in Q2. The milestone underscores the company's rapid commercial scaling in the AI market.

cards.title: Anthropic Founders Cash Out $250M Each in IPO
cards.body: All seven Anthropic co-founders plan to sell equal shares in the IPO, netting approximately $250 million each at the midpoint price. The founders maintain control despite the significant cash-out.

cards.title: OpenAI Acquires Odessia Travel Startup
cards.body: OpenAI has acquired Odessia, a travel startup founded by Sonder's Francis Davidson. The company has not yet disclosed its plans for the acquisition.

cards.title: New York AI Safety Law Takes Effect
cards.body: New York's sweeping AI safety law now requires major developers like OpenAI and Anthropic to register and disclose safety practices. Companies must report critical incidents or face penalties.

cards.title: Oura Acquires Counsel Health for $625M
cards.body: Oura has agreed to acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health in a $625 million deal. The acquisition follows Oura's decision to postpone its IPO indefinitely.

cards.title: PSI Uses AI for Scientific Discovery Breakthroughs
cards.body: PSI leveraged an unreleased Anthropic model to solve a fundamental quantum computing question scientists pursued for nearly two decades. The achievement demonstrates AI's potential in scientific research.

cards.title: Britain's Fractile Raises $720M for AI Chips
cards.body: Fractile has secured $720 million in funding, establishing itself as a top-funded player in purpose-built AI chip development. The round accelerates Britain's competitive position in AI infrastructure.

cards.title: CoreWeave Shifts to Customer Prepayments
cards.body: CoreWeave is increasingly requesting upfront customer payments and shorter contracts to fund AI growth, according to Q3 earnings. The company is also borrowing against specific contracts amid funding pressures.

cards.title: Meta's Infrastructure Head Steps Down
cards.body: Santosh Janardhan, Meta's longtime head of infrastructure who joined in 2009, is stepping down from his role. The departure marks a significant change in the company's infrastructure leadership.

cards.title: Databricks' AI Agent Tells Unvarnished Truth
cards.body: Databricks released a revised Genie agent that CEO Ali Ghodsi uses to learn unfiltered feedback across 12,000 employees. The AI provides insights the CEO couldn't otherwise access directly.

cards.title: Plurai Advances AI Agents Using End-to-End Training
cards.body: Plurai is improving AI agent performance by applying the same end-to-end learning approach that advanced self-driving cars. The methodology addresses challenges in probabilistic systems operating in unpredictable environments.

cards.title: Data Center Boom Faces Permitting and Opposition
cards.body: AI data center projects are encountering significant real-world obstacles including local opposition, permitting delays, and electricity scrambles. Many announced projects may never actually be built.

cards.title: Jensen Huang Faces Congressional Briefing Demand
cards.body: House Republicans have called for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to attend a closed-door briefing on his alleged affair with a Chinese spy. Huang must respond by end of day Wednesday.

cards.title: Jensen Huang Accused of Second Affair
cards.body: Jensen Huang faces new accusations of an affair with an Nvidia executive, following earlier admissions about an affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence agent. The scandal continues to escalate.

cards.title: Nvidia Board Prepares to Oust CEO Huang
cards.body: Nvidia's board reportedly is preparing to remove founder and 33-year CEO Jensen Huang as soon as Wednesday evening. The decision comes amid multiple scandal allegations.

cards.title: Jensen Huang Scandal Timeline Unfolds
cards.body: Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese intelligence operative could have ramifications for U.S. national security in AI development. The scandal is impacting the U.S.-China AI competition.

cards.title: Who Could Replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia?
cards.body: With Nvidia having no succession plan and its CEO in crisis, TechCrunch drafted a list of potential successor candidates. The company faces urgent leadership challenges.

cards.title: Nvidia Crisis Tests Corporate Governance Standards
cards.body: Governance experts say the unfolding Nvidia situation is unprecedented in scope and severity. The crisis is reshaping discussions around corporate accountability at major tech firms.

cards.title: Is Bad Behavior Condoned Across Tech Industry?
cards.body: Investment consultants suggest senior tech leaders are aware of misconduct but effectively condone it. The Huang scandal raises broader questions about industry culture and accountability.

cards.title: Data Centers Face Red Tape Post-Election
cards.body: AI data center projects continue facing local opposition and permitting delays following the Blue Wave results. Real-world infrastructure challenges are slowing the AI buildout significantly.

cards.title: Nancy Pelosi's Replacement Ready to Regulate AI
cards.body: California state senator Scott Wiener, who authored AI risk-curbing legislation, won Nancy Pelosi's San Francisco congressional seat. He's now positioned to shape federal AI policy at a critical moment for the industry.

cards.title: The Climate Case for AI Has Not Been Made
cards.body: At the UN climate conference in Turkey, AI is expected to dominate discussions as countries consider its role in climate solutions. However, evidence supporting AI's climate benefits remains unproven and contested.

cards.title: Innovating with AI in Special Chemicals Industry
cards.body: Companies are leveraging AI, cloud computing, and advanced modeling to accelerate innovation in specialty chemicals. The key challenge is connecting these technologies to reliable data and practical manufacturing expertise.

cards.title: TSMC to Invest $1B in Anthropic and OpenAI
cards.body: Taiwan's chipmaking giant TSMC is backing major AI companies with significant investment. This move signals strong industry confidence in the AI sector's growth trajectory.

cards.title: IBM Offers Dual-Processor Quantum System in 2027
cards.body: IBM will provide access to an advanced quantum computing system featuring dual processors next year. This represents a major step forward in making quantum technology accessible to broader users.

cards.title: Google DeepMind Mathematically Verifies Signal's Security
cards.body: Google DeepMind has provided mathematical verification of key components of the Signal messaging protocol. This validates the cryptographic security of one of the most trusted messaging platforms.

cards.title: What Happens When AI Becomes an Oracle?
cards.body: As AI systems grow more sophisticated, mathematics itself faces fundamental questions about how knowledge is validated and applied. The intersection of AI and mathematics is reshaping how we understand computational truth.

cards.title: Grok Build Coding Agent Leaks Confidential Information
cards.body: xAI's Grok Build coding agent exposed sensitive data including information belonging to SpaceX. The incident raises serious concerns about information security in AI-powered development tools.

cards.title: Big Walk Indie Game Uses AI to Fix Bug
cards.body: An indie gaming studio used AI to resolve a technical bug, sparking broader ethical debates in the gaming community. The incident highlights tensions between AI adoption and traditional development practices.
